name: David Lichtenstein
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2016-2025); Hurun Global (2025-2026)
forbes_bio: Real estate mogul David Lichtenstein first racked up $89,000 in credit card debt to purchase a two-story, multi-family home in New Jersey in 1986.
Today his Lightstone Group oversees some 23,000 rental units across 120 properties across 28 states.
Lightstone is also developing a new brand of millenial-focused city hotels with Marriott, called Moxy. Its Times Square location opened in 2017.
In 2007 he paid $7.4 billion in debt and $200 million in equity for Extended Stay America, a chain of mid-priced hotels.
The recession forced Extended Stay into bankruptcy protection; Lightstone later sold 20 malls for $2.3 billion.
forbes_facts: The son of Brooklyn public school teachers, Lichtenstein never went to college.
He got into the real estate business because his 19-year-old wife was pregnant and he thought he could make money quickly.

name: Yair Hamburger
forbes_bio: Yair Hamburger is a controlling shareholder of Harel Insurance, an Israeli insurance and financial services company.
He is one of three siblings - alongside Gideon Hamburger and Nurit Manor - who control Harel through G.Y.N Consulting, the family's privately held company.
Harel, now one of Israel's biggest institutional financial firms, was founded in 1939 and has remained under family control.
Harel manages assets valued at NIS 571 billion ($176 billion) and operates across health, motor, life insurance, pensions and asset management.

name: Gary Tharaldson
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2024-2025); Hurun Global (2020-2026)
forbes_bio: Gary Tharaldson purchased his first Super 8 motel in 1982 in Valley City, North Dakota.
He has since built, owned and operated over 480 hotels, opening one new hotel per month on average over 40 years.
In 2006, he sold 130 hotels to Goldman Sachs for about $1.2 billion, which he reinvested into land and commercial and residential developments.
In 2008, he launched an ethanol facility near Fargo, North Dakota, which produces over 175 million gallons per year.
forbes_facts: Tharaldson once worked as a physical education teacher and insurance salesman.
Tharaldson is the richest person in North Dakota.

name: Jose Ignacio Comenge
forbes_bio: José Ignacio Comenge is a Spanish investor with holdings in beverage, food, and agribusiness sectors.
He inherited and later expanded interests in Coca-Cola bottling businesses and now holds almost 2% and is board member of Coca-Cola Europacific Partners, his most valuable asset.
Comenge, who is an influential figure in the Madrid business community, prefers leveraged, long-term equity positions rather than High-profile business ventures.
Through his investment vehicle, Mendibea 2002, he owns significant but minority stakes in listed companies such as Prim, Ebro Foods, and Cvne.

name: Prasanna Sankar
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2025); Hurun Unicorn founders (2021-2024)
forbes_bio: Prasanna Sankar cofounded human resources software startup Rippling with fellow billionaire Parker Conrad in 2016.
Sankar owns an estimated 9% of the company, which private investors valued at $16.8 billion in May 2025.
Before cofounding Rippling, Sankar served as director of engineering at another human resources software startup Zenefits, which Conrad founded in 2013.
Sankar served as chief technology officer of Rippling until 2020, before leaving to found 0xPPL, which he describes as a decentralized social network for crypto natives, in 2023.
Born in India, Sankar studied computer science at the National Institute of Technology in Tiruchirappalli. He now lives in Singapore.

name: Rajesh Sharma
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2023-2025); Hurun Global (2022-2026)
forbes_bio: Rajesh Sharma gets his wealth from a majority stake in non-banking finance company Capri Global Capital, which he runs.
Mumbai-based Capri offers home loans, construction loans as well as customized business loans for medium and small-scale enterprises.
It has more than 900 branches across India, with a substantial presence in northern and western India.
forbes_facts: Capri Global started as a construction finance company in 2011.
Capri Global forayed into housing finance in 2017.

name: Andrei Rappoport
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2014-2025); Hurun Global (2020-2026)
forbes_bio: Andrei Rappoport worked for two billionaires, Mikhail Fridman and Mikhail Khodorkovsky, before becoming one himself.
Rappoport worked at Fridman's Alfa-Bank for four years, then joined Khodorkovsky's YUKOS-Rosprom before moving to RAO Unified Energy System.
After RAO UES, he bought Georgian Global Utilities and a Georgian water and power company that he then sold to BGEO Group in 2016.
These days he is an investor in more than 50 PE and VC funds. He was an early investor in Datadog and Delivery Hero.
Rappaport has Russian, Israeli, Cyprus and Portuguese citizenship.
forbes_facts: Rappoport is a master of sports in high-speed pistol shooting.
Rappoport decided to start a bank when he was 28 years old, but had no money. Instead he joined Alfa Bank after seeing an ad in the newspaper.

name: Chu Jian
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2021-2025); Hurun Global (2021-2026); Hurun China (2021-2026)
forbes_bio: Chu Jian founded automation products supplier Zhejiang Supcon Technology in 1999.
Chu received his doctorate in engineering from Zhejiang University in 1989.
Supcon is headquartered in the eastern Chinese city of Hangzhou.
